## D01 — Reproduce current application baseline

Scope: SAHA-151. Type: enabler. Disposition: retain-and-verify.

Requirement: As a developer, establish the original source/runtime/test state so new regressions are distinguishable from inherited failures.

Functional specification: read current repository rules; pin main; install pinned dependencies; execute existing documentation, catalogue, lint, types, build, security, unit and affected HTTP/recovery checks. Data/API: no schema or application mutation. Isolated synthetic fixtures only. Record source/config/test hashes, versions and evidence outside Git; no credentials or raw patient data.

NFR: reproducible commands and environment; no production resources. Native checkout currently failed on GitHub DNS. A read-only GitHub-runner baseline is configured in the dedicated workflow; queued/running is not passed.

Acceptance: D01-A1 exact source/runtime recorded; A2 each required command has observed outcome; A3 inherited, candidate and environment failures distinguished. Refusal: D01-N1 missing dependency is blocked, never green; N2 failed assertions are preserved. Rejection: D01-R1 historical counts used as fresh evidence; R2 deployment/provider activation as part of verification.

Tests/release: original documented tools. A baseline pass is engineering-only; no merge or host change. The original full browser regression selection and physical devices remain separate.

### Discovery test and falsification

* Riskiest assumption: Current institutional identity and assignment changes reach every protected read/action without leaving wrong-person access.
* Population/context: Verified ASHA, administrator and identity-steward archetypes in two synthetic tenants.
* Test: Exercise login, guessed-ID reads, reassignment, active-session suspension and reconnect on existing server identity; capture allowed/denied outcomes and revocation timestamps.

Sum of owned-child forecast ranges before unknown shared-reuse savings; excludes external approval/recruitment/observation wait. Do not add child-task estimates to this total or treat it as calendar duration.

### Learning and exit evidence

Recommended formative window: the first two weeks after an authorised bounded release, then each material config change. Compare exact eligible opportunities/completions, avoidable re-entry, correction burden, denied unsafe actions, sync failures and support load with the declared release baseline and source targets. ## User / outcome

As a frontline worker, I want to start visits, follow-ups and screenings from one authenticated workspace, so I can complete eligible programme work without separate vendor logins or copying patient details.

**Scope boundary:** Keep programme eligibility and existing server permissions intact. Today must retain existing drafts, distinguish a failed source request from an empty caseload, and disclose only assigned work; the full multi-programme journey remains broader than D02.

## Canonical scope and hierarchy

Scope ID: SAHA-001; type: functional. Original IDs: BR-UX-01.
CWO references: CWO-002,CWO-019,CWO-023,CWO-031. Decision references: None recorded.
Primary epic: WP03; related work packages: WP03. Source original release(s): R1.
This is one of the 160 reconciled scope items. 1 original requirement(s) map here exactly once.

## Original requirement and acceptance text

### BR-UX-01 — One task entry point

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

The worker shall start a visit, follow-up or screening from one workspace. Eligible programme activities and AI functions shall appear within that task without requiring the worker to select a vendor application.

Acceptance: The approved multi-programme journey completes through one authenticated workspace with no separate AI login or manual transfer of patient details.

## Additional CWO acceptance / refusal criteria

* **CWO-002-AC01 (New acceptance)**: Given current assigned work, Today shows the same permitted task identities as the scoped source, without exposing another worker’s household details.
* **CWO-002-AC02 (New acceptance)**: Given an existing draft for the selected task/person, starting from Today resumes it or clearly identifies the choice without silently duplicating the visit.
* **CWO-002-AC03 (New acceptance)**: Given no assigned work, a useful empty state appears without invented visits or partner promotions.
* **CWO-002-NEG02 (Expected refusal / recovery)**: A failed source request must not be shown as an empty caseload or completed work.
* **CWO-002-RJ01 (Delivery rejection)**: Reject a twelve-module home hidden behind a chatbot.
* **CWO-002-RJ02 (Delivery rejection)**: Reject any implementation that gives the client authority to start out-of-scope work or loses an existing draft.

## Original test scenarios — not executed acceptance

### TC-BR-UX-01-A — One task entry point acceptance

Type: Functional; source role: QA with Frontline worker; fixture: FX-UX-01.
Preconditions: Synthetic tenant A; verified actor with intended scope; relevant pack and connector test profile active; reset fixture before execution.
Steps: 1. Load FX-UX-01. 2. The home screen groups tasks by person and encounter. Provider selection remains behind an eligible capability action. 3. Capture UI/API results and stored receipt or audit evidence.
Expected: The approved multi-programme journey completes through one authenticated workspace with no separate AI login or manual transfer of patient details.
Formal status: Not run; no engineering subset automatically passes this case.

### TC-BR-UX-01-B — One task entry point adverse condition

Type: Negative or recovery; source role: QA with Frontline worker; fixture: FX-UX-01-NEG.
Preconditions: Isolated synthetic tenant; begin from the corresponding acceptance scenario; inject only the named adverse condition.
Steps: 1. Establish the normal precondition. 2. Disable one programme destination while another remains available; the visit remains usable and displays the missing route. 3. Inspect user state, side effects, audit and any recovery queue.
Expected: Disable one programme destination while another remains available; the visit remains usable and displays the missing route. Evidence must show the actual final state and any accountable unresolved work.
Formal status: Not run; no engineering subset automatically passes this case.

### TC-J01 — Multi programme home visit

Type: End to end; source role: Product QA and programme owner; fixture: FX-J01.
Preconditions: Synthetic environment; role ASHA worker; journey-specific providers and destinations configured as test adapters; no live clinical data.
Steps: 1. Open assigned household work and choose one person; the system verifies assignment and shows source freshness.
2\. Confirm the person and start an encounter. Maternal, TB and hypertension packs contribute their eligible questions.
3\. Capture the narrative once. The extractor returns draft fields with source spans; the worker corrects uncertain values.
4\. The question assembler reuses eligible existing facts and asks only unresolved or genuinely distinct questions.
5\. Run eligible AI support where permitted. Present the source facts, independent results and consolidated actions for review.
6\. Confirm the encounter and authorised programme actions. Submit each destination separately and display its receipt.
7\. Assign every open referral or rejected submission to a responsible person or monitored queue.
Inject exception: A destination timeout leaves only that action uncertain. Patient ambiguity stops disclosure. Urgent approved protocol actions take precedence over forms.
Expected: One confirmed encounter; separate accepted or unresolved destination states; no duplicate entry of an eligible shared fact.
Formal status: Not run; no engineering subset automatically passes this case.

## Authorization, error and recovery contract

Current server role/tenant/assignment/purpose, audit and version constraints remain applicable. Before execution, freeze authorised positive behaviour, out-of-scope/changed-authority refusal, invalid input, unavailable dependency, stale version and uncertain-save recovery wherever relevant. Inspect actual code/API/data and inherited failures; preserve targets and no-side-effect guarantees. Do not substitute an assumed UI or reference API catalogue for a current implementation contract.

## Current evidence and readiness

BR-UX-01: source assessment "partial"; target checkpoint R12. Full remaining scope stays open; see authoritative requirements/assessment.tsv and current evidence-map. Remaining: Validate the full journey with two independent real providers and programme destinations.
Canonical item remains Backlog/unqualified. Current local source/assessment may contain bounded implemented components; original formal acceptance is not thereby passed. No named executor, estimate or delivery date is invented.
Related implementation tasks: D02 / <issue id="adfe4945-bb19-47a6-a87d-a2f8c80962fe" href="https://linear.app/aplyd-sandbox/issue/APL-6/d02-open-assigned-work-from-mobile-today">APL-6</issue>. D02 is delivered only within its frozen read-only synthetic gate; no parent acceptance follows. D03 coding is held for planning.

Inspect current reuse and freeze a minimal ready slice before coding; no bulk implementation dispatch. GitHub #188 remains the single delivery controller. Isolated qualified story PRs, final-code CI/review/native approvals and exact hosting/smoke evidence govern delivery.

### Priority, sequence and forecast

### Scenario coverage and evidence contract

* Positive: Run TC-BR-UX-01-A, TC-J01 using the source-named fixture, actor, preconditions and exact Expected oracle; cover start visits, follow-ups and screenings from one authenticated workspace.
* Refusal/adverse: Run TC-BR-UX-01-B; retained source adverse/recovery case: Disable one programme destination while another remains available; the visit remains usable and displays the missing route.. Its source label does not by itself establish refusal coverage.
* Error/recovery refinement: Fail one programme-work source request while an existing draft remains. Show the source failure separately from zero assigned work and preserve the same draft/person identity.
* Authorization refinement: For frontline worker performing “start visits, follow-ups and screenings from one authenticated workspace”: Remove the source actor’s task/record purpose or change person/assignment between preparation and commitment; deny the protected operation at its existing server/action boundary, preserving previously accepted history.

### Proposed per-clause CWO test contracts — original text unchanged

These are recommended synthetic Given/When/measurement expansions, not approved or frozen replacement criteria. The original clause above is the unchanged Then oracle; proposed fixture IDs are not formal catalogue cases and every execution result remains Not run until observed.

**CWO-002-AC01** — proposed fixture `PROP-CWO-002-AC01`; actor: frontline worker.
* Given: Synthetic workers A and B have distinct current assignments; the permitted source projection for A is pinned.
* When: Sign in as A and open Today; compare each displayed task/person identity with A's authoritative projection.
* Then: retain the exact CWO-002-AC01 clause above unchanged.

**CWO-002-AC02** — proposed fixture `PROP-CWO-002-AC02`; actor: frontline worker.
* Given: The selected assigned person/task already has a named durable draft revision.
* When: Open the task from Today and exercise the visible resume/choice path.
* Then: retain the exact CWO-002-AC02 clause above unchanged.
* Measurement: Compare selected person/task/draft IDs before and after; visit count gains no silent duplicate and the existing draft remains identifiable.
* Prohibited effects: Silent duplicate visit, draft loss, reassociation to another person.

**CWO-002-AC03** — proposed fixture `PROP-CWO-002-AC03`; actor: frontline worker.
* Given: The current authenticated projection is successfully returned with no assigned work.

## User / outcome

As a frontline worker, I want to use the site's approved interface, speech and content languages, so I can understand the encounter without changing the meaning of clinical information.

**Scope boundary:** Supported languages and safety-critical translations require the existing qualified review. Names, numeric values and units must survive language changes; field-specific language evaluation remains required.

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

## User / outcome

As a worker reviewing an encounter, I want separate device-save, server-save, review and destination states, so I know which actions succeeded and which still require recovery.

**Scope boundary:** A completion tick cannot imply acceptance by every destination. Local cancellation must preserve accepted external receipts and identify any separately authorised correction or reversal work.

## Canonical scope and hierarchy

Scope ID: SAHA-006; type: functional. Original IDs: BR-UX-06, BR-RULE-04.
CWO references: CWO-004,CWO-005,CWO-006,CWO-016,CWO-022,CWO-026. Decision references: None recorded.
Primary epic: WP03; related work packages: WP03, WP02. Source original release(s): R1.

## Original requirement and acceptance text

### BR-UX-06 — Status that reflects reality

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

The application shall distinguish saved on device, saved on server, awaiting review, submitted, accepted, rejected and unresolved. A general completion tick shall never imply that every destination accepted a record.

Acceptance: Simultaneous success in one programme and failure in another produces separate visible statuses and a specific recovery action.

### BR-RULE-04 — Honest completion and cancellation

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

Local completion, external acceptance and service completion shall be distinct. Cancelling a local task shall not falsely cancel an accepted external transaction; a separate authorised correction or cancellation request is required.

Acceptance: Cancellation after submission reports the actual destination state and generates any remaining reversal task.

* **CWO-004-AC04 (New acceptance)**: Given a valid save, the persisted visit/pack snapshot agrees with the review card and returns an appropriate local/server state.

records.description:
## User / outcome

As a deployment administrator or identity steward, I want to manage verified workforce membership from invitation through removal, so organisation-owned accounts and pending privileged work reflect each user's current role.

**Scope boundary:** Shared credentials are not the operating model. Suspension or role removal stops new online access and actions within five minutes; disconnected-device residual access follows its disclosed offline grant and lock limits.

## Canonical scope and hierarchy

## Original requirement and acceptance text

### BR-ID-01 — Workforce lifecycle

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

The platform shall support invitation or approved import, identity verification, role assignment, activation, suspension, reassignment and removal. Every account shall belong to an accountable organisation; shared credentials shall not be the operating model.

Acceptance: A suspended user's online access and pending privileged actions are revoked within the NFR limit, with offline limits disclosed.

### NFR-09 — Online revocation

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

Role removal or account suspension shall stop new online access and actions within 5 minutes. A disconnected device is constrained by its offline grant and local lock policy; it cannot be promised immediate remote revocation.

Verification: Session, background job and reconnect tests enforce the limit and record the residual offline window.

No additional CWO criterion assigned to this owner; original criteria are retained unchanged.

Formal status: Not run; no engineering subset automatically passes this case.

### TC-NFR-09-A — Online revocation acceptance

## User / outcome

As a frontline worker, I want validation to identify invalid units, implausible values and missing information without inventing answers, so I can correct inputs or use a permitted documented override.

**Scope boundary:** Mandatory checks cannot be silently bypassed. Permitted overrides retain original value, reason and reviewer identity; missing, refused and uncertain inputs stay distinct, and derived values require approved inputs and formula.

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

Range, unit, logical and cross-field checks shall flag implausible or incomplete inputs. A worker may record an unusual confirmed measurement with a reason where policy permits, but cannot silently bypass a mandatory validation.

Acceptance: Invalid units block submission; a permitted override retains the original value, reason and reviewer identity.

### BR-RULE-01 — No invented facts

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

The platform shall never fill an unanswered clinical or programme field with an assumed answer. It may calculate a derived value only where the formula and required inputs are approved and the result is labelled as derived.

Acceptance: Missing, refused and uncertain inputs remain distinguishable across local records, model calls and outgoing submissions.

## User / outcome

As an AI governance owner, I need to manage a capability's deployment-specific lifecycle and isolate trial, shadow and other unapproved outputs, so that only approved capabilities can influence care and suspended versions stop receiving new invocations.

Bounded scope: Track registration through replacement, refusal of provider self-activation, suspension impacts on in-progress work and exclusion of experimental outputs from operational care; no new clinical approval is granted by this item.

## Canonical scope and hierarchy

This is one of the 160 reconciled scope items. 2 original requirement(s) map here exactly once.

## Original requirement and acceptance text

### BR-AI-04 — Capability lifecycle

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

The lifecycle shall cover registered, technically verified, under review, approved for a scope, active, suspended, retired and replaced. Activation shall be deployment-specific and allow trial or shadow status without exposing unapproved results to care.

Acceptance: A provider cannot self-activate; suspension blocks new invocations and identifies in-progress work requiring cancellation or review.

### BR-RULE-07 — No experimental output in care

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

Training, synthetic, shadow or unapproved model results shall be segregated from the operational care record and shall not influence user-visible clinical action lists.

Acceptance: An experimental high-risk result cannot trigger a live referral or patient notification outside an explicitly authorised evaluation protocol.

## User / outcome

As an integration owner, I need to declare each connector's verified capabilities and readiness evidence, so that only receiving-owner-accepted operations can be exposed as live.

Bounded scope: Record owner, exact environment, authentication, matching, resources, versions, receipts, amendments, operational limits and support; unknown or unsupported behaviour remains unavailable.

## Original requirement and acceptance text

### BR-INT-01 — Integration readiness contract

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

Each connector shall record the system owner, permitted read and write operations, identity method, data contract, authorisation, test environment, support contact and operational limits. Unknown capabilities shall remain explicitly unverified.

Acceptance: A connector cannot be labelled live until the receiving owner has accepted its tested scope and production access is enabled.

### BR-INT-20 — EHR connector capability profile

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

Every EHR or HMIS connector shall publish a capability profile covering supported resources or documents, search keys, read and write operations, authentication, patient matching, terminology, versioning, latency, idempotency, receipts, amendments, deletion restrictions and support ownership.

Acceptance: The platform enables only operations declared in the active profile and blocks configuration that assumes unsupported search, update or acknowledgement behaviour.

### BR-INT-04 — Duplicate prevention and uncertain outcomes

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

Retries shall use stable submission identity and destination-supported duplicate controls. Where acceptance is uncertain, the platform shall reconcile before resubmitting or route the case for review.

Acceptance: A timeout after external acceptance does not create a second patient or activity; an unverifiable outcome remains visibly unresolved.

### NFR-05 — Duplicate-safe execution

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

Repeated delivery, retries and replay of the same logical action shall not create duplicate business events where the connector contract supports idempotency or reconciliation. Unsupported cases shall remain unresolved instead of being blindly retried.

Verification: At least 10000 replay and timeout test events produce no duplicate accepted activity in the supported connector fixtures.

## Additional CWO acceptance / refusal criteria

* **CWO-003-AC03 (New acceptance)**: Given a repeated submission with the same operation identity and payload, no second planned replacement or duplicate activity is created.
* **CWO-003-NEG03 (Expected refusal / recovery)**: A reused idempotency key with changed input is refused; a lost acknowledgement does not trigger a fresh-key duplicate.
* **CWO-006-AC02 (New acceptance)**: Given the server committed but the client lost the acknowledgement, recovery identifies the existing effect and does not create a duplicate visit or charge.
* **CWO-006-AC05 (New acceptance)**: After a process restart during reconciliation, the same operation identity and original payload remain available for safe recovery.
* **CWO-006-NEG01 (Expected refusal / recovery)**: A key reused for a different payload is refused with no second effect.
* **CWO-006-NEG03 (Expected refusal / recovery)**: A provider timeout or malformed receipt remains uncertain until an authoritative reconciliation result exists.
* **CWO-006-RJ02 (Delivery rejection)**: Reject blind automatic retries of an uncertain payment, provider request or external record submission.

## User / outcome

As a frontline worker capturing an encounter, I need to receive a saved indicator only after the encrypted local mutation is durably committed, so that I can trust acknowledged work across crash, routine restart and temporary power loss.

## Original requirement and acceptance text

### BR-OFF-02 — Durable local capture

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

The application shall acknowledge a save only after local persistence succeeds. Insufficient storage, database failure or encryption failure shall be shown before the worker believes a record has been saved.

Acceptance: Forced restart and low-storage tests preserve acknowledged data or clearly report that saving did not complete.

### NFR-04 — No loss of acknowledged local work

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

Acknowledged local saves shall survive application crash, routine restart and temporary power loss on supported devices. No record may be marked saved before durable persistence. Device destruction remains outside this guarantee until synchronisation.

Verification: Fault injection recovers all acknowledged records and identifies any unacknowledged inputs as unsaved.

## Additional CWO acceptance / refusal criteria

* **CWO-005-AC02 (New acceptance)**: After a confirmed durable save, force-closing and reopening the supported app/browser restores the same record and reviewed values after authorised unlock.
* **CWO-005-AC03 (New acceptance)**: An interrupted write leaves either the previous committed version or the next committed version, not a partially mixed record.
* **CWO-005-NEG02 (Expected refusal / recovery)**: Quota exhaustion or a failed encryption/write must not return a success receipt.
* **CWO-005-RJ02 (Delivery rejection)**: Reject a restart test that uses only mocked storage but is reported as handset durability.

As a previously authorised frontline worker, I need to access only data and actions allowed by a time-bounded offline grant, so that cached patient records lock when authority expires or cannot be trusted.

Bounded scope: Preserve the source's proposed 24-hour default and approval-dependent extension up to 72 hours; new privileged grants/disclosures stay online-only, and disconnected revocation cannot be claimed instantaneous.

## User / outcome

As a frontline worker reconnecting after an outage, I need to synchronise dependent person, encounter and referral records in valid order with stable command IDs, so that intermittent connectivity cannot create orphan records or replay successful actions.

Bounded scope: Return per-item results and permission checks; preserve the source's 200-record queue, 95 percent eligible structured arrival within 5 minutes target under reference conditions, with media/external acceptance measured separately.

## Canonical scope and hierarchy

## Original requirement and acceptance text

### BR-OFF-05 — Safe synchronisation ordering

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

Dependent records shall synchronise in a valid order, preserving identities and stable submission identifiers. The application shall recover from intermittent connectivity without replaying successful actions.

Acceptance: A new local person, encounter and referral synchronise without orphan records across repeated connection loss and restoration.

### NFR-12 — Synchronisation recovery

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

On stable reconnection, 95 percent of eligible structured records in a 200-record queue shall reach the platform within 5 minutes under reference network conditions. Media and external destination acceptance have separate measures.

Verification: Queue tests measure completion, rejected records, permission rechecks and remaining unresolved items.

## Additional CWO acceptance / refusal criteria

Bounded scope: Explain review/refusal, preserve work for authorised reassignment and prevent dispatch after revoked role or material rule/data change; planning-stage checks alone do not suffice.

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

Queued actions shall be revalidated against current assignment, permissions, patient linkage, protocol and input freshness before execution. A delayed clinical action shall not proceed solely because it was once drafted.

Acceptance: A material rule or data change places the action into review with an explanation instead of silently executing the old plan.

## User / outcome

As an authorised auditor, I want durable evidence of material reads, writes, approvals, AI calls, exports, configuration and privileged access with actor, authority, object, time, outcome and version, so an encounter or exchange can be reconstructed independently.

**Scope boundary:** Ordinary users cannot alter audit history. Designated external writes and privileged changes stop if durable audit cannot be established; local capture retains its permitted local queue. Exchanges must be traced without raw clinical payloads in general logs.

## Canonical scope and hierarchy

Scope ID: SAHA-129; type: functional. Original IDs: BR-SEC-08, NFR-10, NFR-26.

## Original requirement and acceptance text

### BR-SEC-08 — Audit evidence

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

The platform shall record material reads, writes, approvals, AI calls, exports, configuration changes and privileged access with actor, authority, affected object, time, outcome and version. Ordinary users shall not be able to alter audit history.

Acceptance: An auditor reconstructs a selected encounter and submission from evidence without relying on the chat transcript or provider recollection.

### NFR-10 — Audit completeness and timing

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

All mandatory audit events shall be durable before or atomically with the consequential action where feasible. If durable audit cannot be established, external writes and privileged changes shall stop. Local capture may continue with its local audit queue.

Verification: Audit-store failure blocks the designated actions, while recovery preserves event order and detects clock skew.

### NFR-26 — Consent and exchange traceability

Priority: Must; original release: R1.

Every ABDM or direct EHR exchange shall be traceable from user purpose and authority through request, transformation, disclosure or receipt, acknowledgement and final state without placing raw clinical payloads in general application logs.

Acceptance: Verification: Audit reconstruction succeeds for all release exchanges, while log inspection confirms that secrets, tokens and unnecessary clinical content are absent.
